answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The marble holds work receipts rather than names, so the quartz of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on time-locked work history, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Reaching the gale of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
